quotes.text: Travelled to Guanajuato, MX, this past week (first time out of the US(!)), and happy to report it's a magical place! Great culture, great food, and didn't break the bank. Feet still hurt from all the walking.

But it’s really easy to stay too far afield in a blue-collar neighbourhood. 

I feel like 1 km too far changes everything. In Guanajuato, Mexico, I spent so much time getting to everything that it killed my experience.

But I was there for 7 weeks and moved downtown to a funky area with students.

Inept, no experienced managers/administrators left.  Since￼ Guanajuato is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, they are probably at a resort having a great time with their families in between "inspections".  Making the government a huge swamp in the likeness of Trump.

I am in the state of Guanajuato.  There are options here from a bustling city of Querétaro, to the colonial college town of Guanajuato to the artistic and rather famous town of San Miguel de Allende.  San Miguel de Allende is often referred to a “soft landing” place for Americans. (Cont’d)
